def: The MCP transport for remote servers: one HTTP endpoint that receives each JSON-RPC message as a POST and answers with a JSON object or a Server-Sent Events stream.
A long-lived HTTP response that delivers a sequence of text events from server to client, used by MCP for streamed replies and change notifications.
A design in which every request carries its protocol version and client capabilities, so any server replica can answer it without remembering earlier requests.
The MCP method, required of every server in the 2026-07-28 revision, that returns the supported protocol versions, capabilities and identity of a server.
The MCP pattern in which a server ends a request with an input_required result and the client retries it with the answers and an echoed requestState.
An opaque server-minted string that a client echoes on a retry; because it crosses an untrusted client it must be integrity-protected and bound to user, request and expiry.
The role an MCP server plays in authorisation: it validates access tokens issued by a separate authorisation server and checks their audience and scope.
A document (RFC 9728) that an MCP server publishes to name the authorisation servers able to issue tokens for it.
The resource parameter (RFC 8707) by which a client names the MCP server a token is for, so the token is bound to that audience.
Re-authorising with a larger scope set after a server answers 403 insufficient_scope, keeping the scopes already granted.
A component that uses its own authority on behalf of a caller who lacks it, such as an MCP server forwarding a user's token to another API.
A JSON description hosted at an HTTPS URL that a client uses as its client id, replacing per-client registration with the authorisation server.
A client that tries a modern stateless MCP request first and falls back to the initialize handshake when the server turns out to be legacy.
